responsibility: The main recursive-descent parser for C++. It sits on top of the cp_lexer token stream, recognizes the full C++ grammar and many GNU/C++ extensions, constructs preliminary ASTs and declarations, coordinates with semantic helpers for templates, concepts, contracts, coroutines, OpenMP constructs, linkage specifications, and implicit template parameters, and owns parser state and recovery behavior throughout source parsing. It is the relevant file when the compiler misclassifies source tokens, chooses the wrong grammar production, mishandles tentative parsing or matching delimiters/symbols, or builds the wrong front-end node before later semantic checks run.
same_name_distinction: Contains the full recursive-descent parsing implementation on top of the lexer/token structures, with grammar recognition, parser control flow, deferred processing, and recovery logic. Unlike parser.h, it is the parser algorithm implementation rather than the structural definitions of tokens, lexer state, and parser state.
